prompt.context_jp: ここにひとりの女性チーフが着任してから、営業所の空気___大きく変わってしまった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 営業所の空気___大きく変わってしまった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the narrator's framing of the branch atmosphere.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is commenting *about* the branch atmosphere as the established topic of this opening paragraph — は marks it as the theme being discussed.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would frame 'the atmosphere' as brand-new information being introduced, but the narrator is already leading us into a reflection about this known setting.

prompt.context_jp: 「私___三軒家万智」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私___三軒家万智」
prompt.prompt_en: Sangenya introduces herself to the office. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Standard self-introduction: 'As for me, I'm Sangenya Machi.' は establishes 私 as the topic the predicate describes.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私が三軒家万智 would sound like identifying which person is Sangenya ('I'm the one who is Sangenya'), as if answering 'Who is Sangenya?'

contrast_examples.en: I'm Tanaka (the one you're looking for).

prompt.context_jp: 「私___売れない家はありません！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私___売れない家はありません！」
prompt.prompt_en: Sangenya's catchphrase. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 私に marks Sangenya as the agent/experiencer for whom no unsellable house exists — a set phrase using に with 〜ない (ありません).
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 私 the grammatical subject of ない in a way that clashes with 家はありません (家 is already the は-marked topic). を doesn't fit ある/ない at all.

contrast_examples.jp: 私に分からないことはない。
彼にできないことはない。

prompt.context_jp: やがて、ひとつの見出し___目に飛び込んできた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ひとつの見出し___目に飛び込んできた。
prompt.prompt_en: A headline suddenly catches Niwano's eye. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The headline is new information appearing in the scene — が marks the sudden, newly-perceived subject of 飛び込んできた.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 'the headline' as an already-known topic, but we're meeting it for the first time at this dramatic moment.

prompt.context_jp: そのとき、デスクの電話___けたたましく鳴り響いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: デスクの電話___けたたましく鳴り響いた。
prompt.prompt_en: The phone suddenly rings. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: A sudden event introducing a new subject into the scene — が is standard for events that just happen ('the phone rang').
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the phone a known topic being described, losing the sense of an abrupt, scene-changing event.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家の棒だけ___突き抜け、ほかの営業部員の数字___びっこを引くようにその後ろをついていくばかりだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: ほかの営業部員の数字___びっこを引くようにその後ろをついていくばかりだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Only Sangenya's bar stands out; the others lag behind. Pick the particle for 'the others' numbers'.

feedback.correct_en: Contrastive は: Sangenya's bar is one way, but the others' numbers (in contrast) just limp along behind.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark new information neutrally, but the sentence is clearly setting up a contrast against 三軒家の棒だけ.

contrast_examples.jp: 兄は背が高いが、弟は低い。
contrast_examples.en: My older brother is tall, but my younger brother is short. (contrast)
My younger brother is short. (neutral/new info)

prompt.context_jp: 「あの… 事故物件に住んでおられるのも 家を売るためですか？」「それ___ 安いからです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「それ___ 安いからです」
prompt.prompt_en: Sangenya replies about why she lives in a stigmatized property. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: それは picks up 'living in the stigmatized property' as the topic from Niwano's question and provides the reason — a natural topical response.
feedback.incorrect_en: それが would sound like identifying which thing is the reason ('That's what it is'), odd here since Niwano asked why, not which.

prompt.context_jp: 「一家8人 惨殺事件___ 家だからです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「一家8人 惨殺事件___ 家だからです」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle linking 'a family of 8 murdered' to '家'.

feedback.correct_en: の links the noun phrase: 'the house of/where the 8-person massacre happened'. It modifies 家 attributively.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 事件 a topic independent of 家, breaking the noun-phrase structure. を doesn't fit — だ follows.

contrast_examples.en: It's the house of the incident.
The incident is from long ago.

prompt.context_jp: フロアには庭野の机の明かりだけ___残った。
prompt.prompt_jp: フロアには庭野の机の明かりだけ___残った。
prompt.prompt_en: Only the light at Niwano's desk is left. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: With 〜だけ emphasizing 'only X', が highlights that single, exhaustive subject that remained — it's the one and only thing left.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would shift to a contrastive nuance ('at least only this'), which doesn't match this quiet narrative description of what remains.

prompt.context_jp: その背中に、三軒家の視線___まっすぐ注がれていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 三軒家の視線___まっすぐ注がれていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Sangenya's gaze was fixed on Mika's back. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: A descriptive scene introducing Sangenya's gaze as new/perceived information — が for the observed subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'Sangenya's gaze' a known topic, but the narrator is zooming in on it as a fresh image in the scene.

contrast_examples.en: A gaze was fixed on it. (scene description)

prompt.context_jp: 「いいかげんなヤツ___ 嫌いだからです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「いいかげんなヤツ___ 嫌いだからです」
prompt.prompt_en: Sangenya explains why she's hard on Mika. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: With emotion adjectives like 嫌い, が marks the object of the feeling — 'sloppy people are what I hate'.
feedback.incorrect_en: は could appear in explicit contrast ('As for sloppy people, I hate them'), but the default pattern with 嫌い/好き is が, and no contrast is set up here.

prompt.context_jp: 「良樹___20年間ずっと⇒ 2階に引きこもったままなんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「良樹___20年間ずっと 2階に引きこもったままなんです」
prompt.prompt_en: Izumi finally confesses about her son. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Yoshiki is now the topic she's about to tell them about — は establishes him as the subject of this long-withheld confession.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would merely identify who has been shut in (as if answering 'who?'), but here Izumi is announcing a topic she wants to explain.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家の後___こっそりつけ、彼女が入っていった屋敷の住所を調べずにはいられなかったのだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 三軒家の後___こっそりつけ…
prompt.prompt_en: Niwano secretly followed Sangenya. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 後をつける ('to tail/follow someone') is a fixed collocation taking を for the thing being followed.
feedback.incorrect_en: に or で don't form this idiom. 後に would mean 'after' (time) and 後で would mean 'later'.

prompt.context_jp: 周りの物音も耳___入らないほど、庭野は画面に集中していた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 周りの物音も耳___入らないほど…
prompt.prompt_en: The sounds didn't reach his ears. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 耳に入る ('to reach one's ears') uses に to mark the destination/goal of the sound entering.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would make 耳 a direct object (ungrammatical with 入る here). で (location of action) doesn't fit a motion/arrival verb.

prompt.context_jp: その夜、屋代は行きつけのバー「ちちんぷいぷい」の扉___くぐった。
prompt.prompt_jp: バー「ちちんぷいぷい」の扉___くぐった。
prompt.prompt_en: Yashiro went through the bar's door. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: くぐる takes を to mark the thing one passes through — the doorway is the path traversed.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a destination, but くぐる focuses on the act of passing through, not arriving at.

prompt.context_jp: 真夏の日差しがアスファルトを照りつけ、額___はじっとりと汗がにじんでくる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 額___はじっとりと汗がにじんでくる。
prompt.prompt_en: Sweat seeps onto her forehead. Pick the particle before は.

feedback.correct_en: にじむ takes に to mark the surface/location where something seeps out onto — 'sweat seeps onto the forehead'.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks the location of an action, but にじむ is about appearance on a surface, which に captures. を doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.en: Tears well up in the eyes.

prompt.context_jp: 「私の心配をするより 家を___なさい」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私の心配をするより 家を___なさい」
prompt.prompt_en: Sangenya tells Niwano to focus on work. Pick the verb.

feedback.correct_en: Sangenya's whole mantra is 家を売る ('sell houses'). She's redirecting Niwano back to his real job.
feedback.incorrect_en: 買う (buy) and 借りる (rent) are the customer's side — a real estate salesperson's imperative is to sell.

contrast_examples.en: A customer who buys a house.

prompt.context_jp: 心臓が___と音を立て、言い訳の言葉がひとつも出てこない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 心臓が___と音を立て…
prompt.prompt_en: His heart was pounding. Pick the mimetic word.

feedback.correct_en: どくどく is the standard mimetic for a heart pounding heavily — fits the moment Niwano is caught looking at the murder article.
feedback.incorrect_en: さらさら describes smooth flowing (water, hair); きらきら is sparkling. Neither matches a startled, racing heartbeat.

prompt.context_jp: 「お___ください 2軒まとめて 私が売ります」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「お___ください 2軒まとめて 私が売ります」
prompt.prompt_en: Sangenya accepts the sales job confidently. Pick the word.

feedback.correct_en: お任せください ('Leave it to me') is the set business phrase expressing confident acceptance of a client's request.
feedback.incorrect_en: お疲れ(様)is a greeting for finished work; お願いください would mean 'please request' (nonsensical from a service provider).

contrast_examples.jp: よろしくお願いします。
contrast_examples.en: Please take care of it. (from the asker)

prompt.context_jp: 尾行など褒められたことではないと分かってはいたが、好奇心のほうが___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 好奇心のほうが___。
prompt.prompt_en: Curiosity won out over his sense of restraint. Pick the verb.

feedback.correct_en: 〜のほうが勝つ is the idiom for 'X wins out over Y' — curiosity beat his better judgment.
feedback.incorrect_en: 負けた would mean curiosity lost (opposite meaning). 落ちた doesn't form this idiom.

prompt.context_jp: 予算を上げてもらうための言葉を、何度も頭の中で___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 何度も頭の中で___。
prompt.prompt_en: Niwano mentally rehearses his pitch. Pick the verb.

feedback.correct_en: 繰り返す ('to repeat') fits mentally rehearsing the same words again and again.
feedback.incorrect_en: 折り返す means 'to turn back/call back'; 引き返す means 'to retrace steps'. Neither captures mental repetition.

prompt.context_jp: 「わざわざ いらしていただいて すいません」「___ございません ステキな玄関ですね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___ございません ステキな玄関ですね」
prompt.prompt_en: Niwano politely deflects the host's thanks. Pick the phrase.

feedback.correct_en: とんでもございません ('not at all') is the polite deflection to someone thanking or apologizing to you.
feedback.incorrect_en: 申し訳ございません means 'I'm sorry' — wrong when the client is thanking you. ありがとうございません isn't a phrase.

contrast_examples.en: Not at all / Don't mention it.

prompt.context_jp: 「予算も変だし 2階に___間があるし⇒ 何か おかしいな」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「2階に___間があるし」
prompt.prompt_en: Niwano senses something off about the upstairs room. Pick the modifier.

feedback.correct_en: 開かずの間 is a set phrase for 'a room that is never opened' — exactly the mystery room upstairs.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other forms aren't established expressions; 開かず uses the classical negative of 開く (intransitive 'to open') locked into this idiom.

prompt.context_jp: 「あなたは 物事の___しか 見ていない」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あなたは 物事の___しか 見ていない」
prompt.prompt_en: Sangenya scolds Mika for narrow thinking. Pick the word.

feedback.correct_en: 物事の一面しか見ていない ('seeing only one side of things') is the fixed phrase Sangenya uses to criticize Mika's narrow view.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一度 is 'one time'; 一方 means 'one direction/the other party', not the 'side/aspect' of a matter.

contrast_examples.en: See one side of the problem.

prompt.context_jp: 「今の家が 5000万で売れそうなら⇒ もっと高い物件 うまく___」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「もっと高い物件 うまく___」
prompt.prompt_en: The boss tells Niwano to upsell. Pick the verb.

feedback.correct_en: 薦める ('to recommend') is the sales verb — pitch a pricier property to the client.
feedback.incorrect_en: 止める (stop) and 諦める (give up) would mean dropping the deal, the opposite of what the boss wants.

prompt.context_jp: Sangenya introducing herself and her signature line.
prompt.prompt_en: Which pairing sounds most natural for Sangenya's self-introduction + catchphrase?

choices.text: 「私は三軒家万智。」/「私に売れない家はありません！」
「私が三軒家万智。」/「私は売れない家はありません！」
「私を三軒家万智。」/「私が売れない家はありません！」

feedback.correct_en: は for topic self-introduction; に for the agent in '〜に売れない家はない' idiom. This is how Sangenya actually says it in the show.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私が三軒家 would answer 'who is Sangenya?' (odd as self-intro). 私はで売れない家はありません is ungrammatical structure.

contrast_examples.jp: 私に無理なことはない。

prompt.context_jp: Sangenya cutting off Niwano's worry about her.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version best matches Sangenya's blunt, chief-to-junior tone?

choices.text: 「私の心配をするより 家を売りなさい」
「私のことを心配してくれるより、家を売ってくださいませんか」

feedback.correct_en: 〜なさい is the firm, superior-to-subordinate command fitting a chief addressing her junior salesman — exactly Sangenya's register.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is overly polite (clashes with her persona). C is too crude/barked — not her cool, formal-but-cutting style.

prompt.context_jp: Sangenya promising to find a hideaway home for the hikikomori son.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for her professional pledge?

choices.text: 「息子さんが世間に出ないで済む 引きこもりの城を お探しします」
「息子さんが世間に出なくていい 引きこもりの城を 探してあげます」
「息子さんの世間に出ないの 引きこもりの城を 探します」

feedback.correct_en: 〜ないで済む ('get by without having to') + humble お探しします is the natural, professional phrasing to a client.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's 探してあげます sounds condescending toward a client. C mangles the noun-modifying structure.

contrast_examples.en: A way to get by without going.

prompt.context_jp: Adachi explaining why real-estate photos matter.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for his advice about taking listing photos?

choices.text: 「一番いい写真を心を込めて 撮ってあげないといけないんだ」
「一番いい写真を心が込めて 撮らなきゃいけない」
「一番いい写真で心を込めて 撮ってあげないと」

feedback.correct_en: 心を込めて ('with heartfelt care') takes を — the heart is what you put *into* the action. Natural, warm advice-giving tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 心が込めて is ungrammatical (心が込める doesn't work). 写真で would make the photo the means, not the object taken.

prompt.context_jp: Mama Kokoro's magic chant to cheer Yashiro up at the bar.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version matches the warm, playful bar-mama tone?

choices.text: 「つらいの つらいの 飛んでいけ～！ ちちんぷいぷい ぷいぷいぷい～！」
「つらさよ、どうか飛んでいってください。ちちんぷいぷい。」
「つらいが つらいが 飛んでいく ちちんぷいぷい」

feedback.correct_en: The 'X の X の 飛んでいけ' pattern is the classic nursery-style charm — intimate, playful, exactly a mama's comforting chant.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is too stiffly polite for a bar chat. C uses が and plain 飛んでいく, breaking the sing-song imperative of the real chant.

contrast_examples.jp: 痛いの痛いの飛んでいけ。
